topic: What happens if you fall into a black hole
script: If you fell into a black hole, you could be stretched out like spaghetti. Gravity would pull much harder on your feet than on your head, and the difference grows as you fall. Scientists really call this spaghettification. But at a giant supermassive black hole, you could cross the edge without feeling a thing. To a friend watching from far away, you would seem to slow down and fade, never quite falling in. Follow WonderBytes for more facts that sound fake but are true.

description:
Near a small black hole, gravity pulls far harder on your feet than your head, stretching you out. Scientists call it spaghettification. At a supermassive black hole, the stretching is gentle enough at the edge that you could cross it without noticing, while anyone watching from afar would see you slow down, redden and fade.
